text: People don't quit the game. They quit organizing it. Six messages, and still no game.
This is Serve. Your agent agrees your week with your friends' agents, and you say yes once. It runs on Muse Glimmer, on my own RTX 3090.

Act one: cold start. I ask my agent for one more player on Saturday. Muse Glimmer drafts the invite with the nearest court, and Llama Guard checks it before anyone sees it. I post it, and share the link to any group chat.
Leo has no account. The link opens the game, one sign-in, and he's in. The game is full, and I hear: game on.

Act two: agents negotiate. One tap plans my week. Each friend's agent answers over A2A, with signed Agent Cards. A small model I fine-tuned answers when it's sure, and Glimmer when it's not. Everyone agreed, and nothing is booked until I say yes.
Or in Messenger: one yes, and it's booked.
And it's a real negotiation: Hana's agent counter-offers Saturday.

Act three: courts and clubs. Real courts from OpenStreetMap. Prompt Guard screens the reviews first, then Glimmer judges every court, and each reason cites the map, a review or the forecast. Clubs sit on a real map too, and anyone can start one.
Beyond text: your own video, auto-cut into a clip to share with your club.
Fifteen Meta models. Six carry Serve, with Muse Glimmer at the centre.
Glimmer needs forty seconds. The 1B model I fine-tuned on its choices needs under one, and agrees 89.5 percent of the time.
Ninety-three attacks, all stopped, under Meta's Agents Rule of Two.
It's live, with real players and two real clubs.
And it works for school clubs, older adults, a charity cup: any ball sport.
